title: Reading Corner January Newsletter on Fluency
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
TITLE 

TALK 

CORNER

TITLE TALK CORNER

summary:
The January Reading Corner newsletter focuses on **reading fluency** - the ability to read accurately, at an appropriate pace, and with expression. Fluency develops through regular reading and rereading of books and passages, not just memorizing sight words. **Simple ways families can support fluency include:**
- Read and reread familiar books, stories, or short passages
- Practice sight words as part of reading, not just in isolation
- Read aloud to model smooth, expressive reading
- Talk briefly about the story to support understanding

**Helpful resource:** Reading Rockets offers family-friendly tips and videos for supporting fluent reading at home. Contact your student's Reading Corner Teacher for help with these activities.

title: Health Reminder: Flu and Seasonal Illness Protocol
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
NURSE'S 

CORNER

NURSE'S CORNER

summary: The school is experiencing an increase in flu and seasonal illnesses. **Keep your child home if they have:** fever (100°F or higher), vomiting or diarrhea, significant cough, sore throat with fever, body aches, extreme fatigue, or flu-like symptoms. Students must be **fever-free for 24 hours without medication** and **symptom-free for 24 hours after vomiting or diarrhea** before returning to school.

title: Head Lice Check Before School Break
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
NURSE'S 

CORNER

NURSE'S CORNER

Dear Parents and Guardians,As we head into the upcoming school break, I kindly ask that you take a few minutes to check your child's head for signs of head lice. School breaks, gatherings and sleepovers are a common time for lice to spread, and early detection and treatment helps us maintain a healthy school environment for all students.If you find any signs of lice or nits, please begin treatment before your child returns to school. Feel free to contact me if you have any questions or need guidance. There is also information about head lice on the school website, under "Departments" then click "School Nursing Offices". Thank you for your support and cooperation!Tonja Fangman, BSN, RN, LSNDistrict Nursefangmant@talawanda.org

summary: The district nurse requests that parents check their children for head lice before returning from the upcoming school break. Lice commonly spread during breaks, gatherings, and sleepovers, so early detection and treatment is important. If lice or nits are found, please treat before returning to school. Additional information is available on the school website under **Departments > School Nursing Offices**. Contact: Tonja Fangman, BSN, RN, LSN at fangmant@talawanda.org.
